holidays.name: National Cream-Filled Donut Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the donut with a surprise inside. Think custard, vanilla cream, or Boston cream, and the first bite that makes you go "ooh." Grab one for yourself and a few extra to share with friends.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance, and nobody has pinned down who started it. Filled pastries go back to European bakeries centuries ago. Immigrants and bakers later carried the idea to America, where filled donuts became a bakery-case favorite.
holidays.funFact: A donut with no hole is usually the filled kind. The hole would let the cream leak out, so filled donuts are made as solid rounds and injected with filling after frying.

holidays.name: National Eat a Hoagie Day
holidays.description: This day is for the sandwich that goes by many names: hoagie, sub, grinder, hero, or torpedo. Pile cold cuts, cheese, crisp lettuce, tomato, and a drizzle of oil and vinegar onto a long roll. Then argue with your friends about what to call it.
holidays.origin: The hoagie is closely tied to Philadelphia. One popular story traces it to Italian-American workers and sandwich makers in the city in the early 1900s. The date is an unofficial food observance, and its creator is unknown.
holidays.funFact: Philadelphia's hoagie origin story is still debated. Some versions credit workers at the Hog Island shipyard, and others credit local Italian-American delis. Every sandwich-loving region has its own name for the sandwich and its own opinion on the topic.

holidays.name: National Hug Your Hound Day
holidays.description: A tail-wagging day for dog lovers to give their canine pals extra snuggles, belly rubs, and treats. Any dog counts, whether it's a basset, a beagle, or a lovable mutt.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a popular excuse to give your dog some bonus attention.
holidays.funFact: Hugs aren't every dog's favorite thing. Many dogs prefer a good chest scratch or a belly rub, so watch your hound's body language and let them set the pace.
